ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
The speaker seeks the dust of the feet of the saints and applies it to the forehead as a mark of supreme humility and surrender. This physical act symbolizes internalizing the wisdom and virtues of the devout, treating their company as the ultimate wealth and spiritual perfection. It is a declaration that true treasure lies not in material gain but in the sanctifying grace found in sangat.

ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
The speaker pleads for the dust from the feet of the Guru's Sikhs, a concrete image representing the sanctifying power of sangat (the company of the devout). This request acknowledges the speaker's own sinful state and seeks spiritual elevation through association with the enlightened. The dust is not mere dirt but a symbol of humility and the transformative grace found in the presence of the holy. By asking for this blessing, the sinner hopes to attain a high spiritual state and ultimate liberation.

ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
The speaker prostrates before humble devotees and anoints their own face with the dust of the saints' feet, expressing radical humility and the desire to internalize the spiritual grounding found in sangat (the company of the devout). This act of reverence seeks to erase ego by physically and mentally submitting to those who sing divine virtues, aiming to join them in praising the Creator and absorb their sanctified state through contact with their path.

Themes: prostration, humility, dust of feet, sangat, devotees, surrender, ego eradication, divine praise
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
The speaker declares an intent to perform humble service for a devotee of the Divine, specifically wiping dust from the devotee's feet with their own hair. This act of extreme self-abasement and reverence treats the servant of God as the direct object of worship, illustrating that serving the devout is equivalent to serving the Divine itself. The imagery of using hair to clean feet signifies total surrender and the erasure of ego through physical humility.

Themes: service of the devout, humility, self-abasement, reverence for the holy, surrender of ego, physical devotion, treating the guru as god, dust of feet
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The speaker petitions the Divine for grace to obtain the dust from the feet of the saints, treating this physical dust as the ultimate symbol of humility and the true source of spiritual peace. This plea equates the comfort of the soul with the act of surrendering to the sangat (company of the devout), framing the yearning for connection with holy beings as the only remedy for inner unrest. The request is for the specific blessing of lowering oneself before the enlightened to find tranquility.

Themes: divine grace, dust of the feet, sangat, humility, spiritual peace, yearning, surrender, saints
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
The speaker pleads for total physical prostration before the sangat (company of the devout), desiring that the forehead touch their feet, the eyes gaze upon their blessed vision, and the body be covered in the dust of their feet. This intense imagery of surrender expresses a longing to humble the ego completely and find refuge in the holy presence, equating the dust of the saints with spiritual purification and the ultimate grounding of the self.

ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
The supremely beautiful Enticer and Beloved pervades all creation yet remains utterly distinct and transcendent. This paradox declares the Divine’s simultaneous immanence within the world and transcendence beyond it. Words of praise and remembrance grant spiritual life, linking the soul to the One who captivates the heart. The speaker adores the Lord who is both intimately present in everything and uniquely separate from everything.

Themes: divine immanence, transcendence, paradox of unity and separation, praise as life-giving, captivation of the heart, spiritual vitality, remembrance, supreme beauty
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
The speaker exalts the Divine by declaring that naam (the divine Name), physical form, and spiritual color are all profoundly beautiful. This is an act of intense admiration and praise, acknowledging that the Lord’s essence, appearance, and love are supremely attractive. The repetition emphasizes that every aspect of the Beloved is lovely, inviting the mind to dwell on this splendor and find satisfaction in the Lord's alluring nature.

ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
The Divine is addressed as beautiful and the source of all nectar, meaning the essence of all flavors or relishable experiences. This declaration praises the Creator's supreme attractiveness and role as the origin of all spiritual delight and satisfaction. It identifies the Divine as the fountain from which every taste and joy flows, affirming that all pleasurable essence originates from this singular, beautiful Source.

Themes: divine beauty, source of nectar, essence of all flavors, spiritual delight, origin of joy, praise of the Creator, supreme attractiveness, fountain of satisfaction
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The soul addresses the Divine as a beloved Master whose sight alone captivates the heart. Seeing the Lord’s form brings a state of spiritual intoxication and ecstatic absorption, where the mind is overwhelmed by divine beauty. This vision of the Beloved enraptures the devotee, inducing a trance-like joy that transcends ordinary perception. The act of gazing upon the Divine presence results in complete fascination and a loss of self in the wonder of the Lord.

Themes: divine beauty, spiritual intoxication, ecstatic vision, divine gaze, absorption in the Lord, fascination, enraptured soul, beholding the Beloved
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The radiant splendor of the compassionate Lord of the Universe, the beloved Gopal, is supremely beautiful and manifests within the home of mercy. This infinite, boundless glory is visually resplendent and spiritually overwhelming, declaring that the Divine’s presence is an endless, lovely display of grace. The text praises the limitless nature of this beauty, emphasizing that the Lord’s attractive form and benevolent character are without end or boundary.
Themes: divine splendor, infinite mercy, Gopal as Lord of the Universe, boundless grace, spiritual beauty, limitless nature, compassionate presence, radiant glory.
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine personally protects and honors His own servants, taking full responsibility for their preservation. He Himself inspires and enables them to engage in the simran (loving remembrance) of naam (the divine Name), indicating that devotion is not a human achievement but a grace initiated and sustained by the Creator. The Lord guards the devotee and simultaneously motivates the practice of chanting His Name.

Themes: divine protection, grace, naam, simran, servitude, divine initiative, self-sustaining devotion, honor.
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Supreme Being safeguards the honor and dignity of the humble devotees, preserving their spiritual standing across all eras. This divine protection is not a one-time event but a continuous, historical reality spanning every age, ensuring that the sanctity of those who surrender is never compromised. The Lord acts as an eternal guardian, maintaining the respect and high status of the faithful throughout time.
Themes: divine protection, preservation of honor, eternal guardianship, devotee dignity, continuity across ages, historical faithfulness, spiritual safeguarding, humble service
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
The Divine is addressed as the Master of life and the Beloved Lord, emphasizing a relationship of mutual affection where the devotees belong to the Creator and the Creator is dear to the devotees. This reciprocal love establishes that the Lord is the cherished one of the devout, binding them together through shared devotion and intimate connection. The stance is one of declaring the beloved nature of the Divine as the central reality for the faithful.

Themes: mutual love, divine beloved, master of life, reciprocal affection, devotee, intimate connection, cherished lord, belonging to god
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
The Eternal Creator is the sole refuge and sustaining support for devotees and saints, meaning the divine Name itself is the only shelter and reliance for the devout. This declaration identifies the True Lord as the protector and helper, establishing that spiritual safety and strength come exclusively from the Creator rather than worldly means. The verse affirms that the divine Name functions as the ultimate sanctuary and backbone for the faithful.

Themes: divine refuge, eternal support, reliance on naam, protection for saints, sanctuary, true creator, spiritual strength, devotee's shelter
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine continually creates devotees across all ages and actively safeguards their honor and dignity, especially during times of crisis or oppression. This action demonstrates a perpetual commitment to protecting the sanctity of the faithful, ensuring that their spiritual standing remains intact regardless of external circumstances. It affirms that the preservation of the devotee's respect is an ongoing, timeless function of the Lord.

Themes: divine protection, preservation of honor, creation of devotees, timeless support, crisis intervention, dignity, divine sovereignty, guardianship.
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
The speaker pleads with the Master to overlook past deeds, asking that Divine grace override the strict accounting of karma (cause and effect). This is a request for protection based on the relationship of servant to Lord, where the Master preserves the servant's honor rather than punishing them. The prayer seeks refuge in the Divine's nature, emphasizing that salvation depends on the Lord's mercy, not the individual's actions.
Themes: divine mercy, grace over karma, servant-master relationship, surrender, protection of honor, disregard for past deeds, reliance on the Lord.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
The human being must adopt the posture of a beggar to request the divine Name, and the Master accepts this plea. Continual asking for naam (the divine Name) transforms the soul into a supplicant who receives the Lord's acceptance. The act of imploring the Creator for the Name is itself granted by the Owner, establishing a relationship where the devotee petitions and the Divine approves the request for spiritual connection.

Themes: divine Name, begging, supplication, acceptance, continual request, Lord and Master, spiritual poverty, granted prayer
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
Grant the gift of naam (the divine Name) to instill true contentment, thereby extinguishing the burning hunger of the mind. This plea seeks spiritual sustenance that replaces inner craving with deep satisfaction, asking the Divine to fulfill the soul's insatiable desire through the blessing of remembrance. The request connects the reception of the Name with the cessation of mental thirst and the arrival of lasting peace.

Themes: naam (the divine Name), santokh (contentment), mental hunger, spiritual fulfillment, cessation of craving, divine gift, inner satisfaction, extinguishing thirst.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
This destitute soul repeatedly implores the Divine Master, the refuge and sustainer of all beings, to grant the gift of naam (the divine Name). The speaker adopts the posture of a beggar, emphasizing total dependence and the urgent need for spiritual sustenance over worldly gain. It is a plea for the only treasure that endures, asking the Lord of all life to bestow the ultimate fulfillment.

Themes: divine Name, begging for grace, spiritual poverty, dependence on God, refuge, prayer, supplication, inner longing
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
The speaker pleads for divine grace to enable the chanting of naam (the divine Name), acknowledging that remembrance is only possible through God's support. Addressing the Lord as the Sustainer of life and Master of the universe, this prayer requests assistance rather than demanding it, emphasizing that loving repetition depends entirely on the recipient receiving mercy. It frames spiritual practice as a gift granted by the Creator, not a self-generated act.

Themes: divine grace, chanting naam, prayer for assistance, surrender, remembrance, dependence on God, mercy, simran
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
The soul, a destitute supplicant, pleads for the limitless treasure of the divine Word (shabad) rather than material aid. This petition frames spiritual wisdom as the only true sustenance, asking the Beloved to bestow this gift out of love. It redefines begging as a noble pursuit of the Creator’s infinite wealth, emphasizing that the devotee seeks only the grace of hearing and internalizing the eternal sound current.

Themes: begging for divine wisdom, shabad as sustenance, spiritual poverty, petitioning the Beloved, grace of the Guru, seeking the infinite treasure, love as the basis of giving.
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
The speaker adopts the posture of a destitute beggar standing at the Divine portal, pleading for the gift of grace. This is a total surrender of ego, acknowledging that all spiritual wealth comes solely from the Lord's benevolence. The request is not for material gain but for the ultimate charity of mercy and compassion. By asking at the threshold, the devotee emphasizes dependence on the Master's will and the necessity of divine favor for spiritual sustenance.

Themes: divine door, begging for grace, spiritual poverty, surrender, divine mercy, dependence on the Lord, gift of compassion, petitioning the Master.
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
The mind and body blossom and turn green with life upon receiving even a single drop of the Nectar of naam (the divine Name). This transformation is described as a spiritual flourishing where the inner self opens like a flower and the physical frame is revitalized by the water of the soul. A mere taste of this divine essence causes the entire being to thrive, bloom, and become verdant.

ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
Drinking the Lord's sublime essence, or naam-amrit (the nectar of the divine Name), causes the devotee to be permanently dyed in that color. This metaphor of consumption and dyeing signifies that internalizing the divine presence saturates the entire being, leaving one forever imbued, colored, and transformed by the love of the Creator. The act of tasting results in a state of permanent spiritual intoxication and absorption.

Themes: divine essence, naam-amrit, spiritual intoxication, permanent transformation, internalization, divine love, saturation, absorption
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Singing the Lord's praises is the essence of spiritual life, acting as a life-giving elixir that nourishes the soul. This practice of kirtan (devotional singing) generates an unceasing internal resonance, where the celestial sound-current of the naad vibrates continuously within the devotee. Day and night, the instruments of spiritual bliss play inside, filling the being with the ambrosial taste of divine love and unbroken awareness.

Themes: kirtan, naad, spiritual elixir, internal resonance, unceasing remembrance, divine bliss, celestial sound, ambrosial nectar
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
The speaker directly addresses the physical tongue as a beloved companion, commanding it to consume the immortalizing essence of naam (the divine Name) rather than ordinary speech. This personification treats the organ of taste and speech as the primary vehicle for spiritual nourishment, urging it to absorb the life-giving flavor of the divine. The instruction transforms the act of speaking or chanting into an act of internal drinking, where the soul is sustained by the taste of the divine rather than physical food.

Themes: personification of the tongue, drinking the divine Name, spiritual nourishment, immortalizing nectar, internalizing the divine, taste of naam, life-giving essence, command to the self.
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The devotee remains perpetually intoxicated by the flavor of naam, the divine Name, experiencing a spiritual drunkenness that transcends ordinary awareness. This state of absorption functions as a declaration of total immersion in the Lord’s essence, where the soul is overpowered by divine love rather than wine. The servant is lost in the taste of the Lord, finding ecstasy in the sublime essence that acts as a powerful elixir for the consciousness.

Themes: divine intoxication, naam as elixir, spiritual absorption, ecstasy of devotion, flavor of the Lord, intoxication without wine, immersion in divine essence.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Drinking the ambrosial essence through the Guru’s Word grants spiritual life and immortality. This act of internalizing the divine Name transforms the devotee, who then offers their entire self in sacrifice to that Name. The speaker declares total surrender and willingness to be consumed by the object of their devotion, having tasted the life-giving nectar of instruction. Consuming the immortalizing elixir of the Guru’s speech leads to complete self-offering and dedication to the divine identity.

Themes: ambrosial nectar, spiritual immortality, Guru’s Word, self-sacrifice, divine Name, total surrender, internalizing wisdom, life-giving essence
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The divine Name is the supreme essence, the true nectar granting spiritual life, far surpassing all other tastes. The speaker yearns to internalize this ambrosial flavor, asking earnestly by what method or discipline it can be obtained and consumed. This is a desperate plea for the means to taste and assimilate the immortalizing substance of God, seeking the way to drink in the life-giving elixir of the Lord’s identity.

Themes: Naam as nectar, spiritual hunger, longing for God, method of realization, internalizing the divine, supreme essence, life-giving sustenance, seeking the way.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
Drink in the sublime essence of the Lord, O Siblings of Destiny. This imperative urges the absorption of divine bliss through the practice of simran (loving remembrance) while taking refuge in the Perfect Guru. The metaphor of drinking conveys an internalization of the Lord's essence, transforming the devotee by saturating the being with the nectar of naam (the divine Name). It is a call to fully imbibe spiritual wisdom rather than merely hearing it.

Themes: divine essence, internalization, simran, guru refuge, spiritual nectar, absorption, naam, bliss
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
Abandon the insipid water of worldly vices and corruption, which offers no true satisfaction, and instead imbibe the supreme nectar of naam (the divine Name). This instruction urges the mind to reject the bland, fleeting pleasures of maya (worldly attachment) in favor of the intoxicating, enduring spiritual essence found in loving remembrance. The speaker contrasts the dry emptiness of vice with the rich flavor of divine connection, urging a complete exchange of one for the other.

Themes: rejection of vice, insipid world, divine nectar, naam (the divine Name), spiritual intoxication, maya (worldly attachment), exchange of pleasures, inner satisfaction
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
The inner mind houses the venomous snake of separation from the Divine, a pain that no mantra or incantation can subdue or charm. This intense spiritual anguish, born of distance from the Guru, renders all magical formulas and ritual recitations useless. The agony of being apart from the Beloved is a consuming poison that ordinary religious remedies cannot cure or control.

Themes: separation from God, inner anguish, failure of rituals, futility of mantras, spiritual pain, Guru's refuge, uncontrollable mind, venomous longing
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
The speaker addresses their mother to declare that existence is impossible without the Divine, framing life as unbearable separation rather than mere biological survival. This rhetorical question emphasizes that the soul's vitality depends entirely on the divine Name, transforming a plea into a statement of total dependence where living without the Beloved is tantamount to spiritual death. The anguish of separation reveals that true consciousness is sustained only by connection with the Supreme Soul.
Themes: separation from the Divine, dependence on the divine Name, spiritual anguish, rhetorical pleading, mother as confidant, vitality of the soul, unbearable existence, connection to the Supreme Soul
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
An intense, loving desire to meet the Divine has awakened within the mind, marking a shift from separation to longing. This internal attachment to the Beloved signifies deep spiritual yearning and the beginning of a quest for union. The mind is now captivated by the thought of meeting God, replacing worldly concerns with a singular focus on divine connection and the emotional pull of reunion.

Themes: divine union, spiritual longing, loving remembrance, internal awakening, attachment to God, yearning for the Beloved, emotional devotion, separation from the Divine
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
The mind burns with agonizing separation, craving the sight of the Divine just as a parched body perishes without water. This simile portrays spiritual longing as a desperate physical thirst, emphasizing that the soul cannot exist without beholding the Lord. The intense yearning for darshan (seeing the Divine) is equated with the vital need for water, showing that the vision of God is essential for life.

Themes: spiritual thirst, darshan, longing, separation, simile, burning, divine sight, essential need
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
Without the Divine Husband, no one inquires into this soul’s welfare or asks after its life. The soul cries out alone in the wilderness of the world, abandoned by all other connections. This image of solitary weeping in a jungle expresses total dependence on the Beloved and the realization that worldly relationships offer no real support or companionship in spiritual separation. The speaker laments isolation while affirming that only the Divine truly cares.

Themes: spiritual isolation, divine husband, worldly abandonment, crying in wilderness, reliance on god, futility of human relationships, separation from beloved.
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
Detachment from worldly concerns arises as the mind fills with love for the Divine, creating an intense yearning to behold the Vision of God's presence. This spiritual longing replaces attachment to maya with a burning desire for darshan, the sight of the Beloved. The soul, now dispassionate toward material existence, craves only the direct experience of the Divine form.

Themes: detachment, divine longing, darshan, love for God, spiritual desire, inner transformation, dispassion, divine vision
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
The soul, separated from the Divine Husband for ages, pleads for reunion within the heart-home. This urgent petition seeks the Lord's presence to dwell inside, facilitated by the Guru's sabad (divine word). The request is for permanent settlement in the inner sanctuary, ending the long exile through the instruction of the true Guru. It is a cry for the Beloved to enter and abide, resolving the pain of prolonged separation through the connecting power of the Word.
Themes: divine union, longing for the Beloved, sabad as connector, inner sanctuary, spiritual separation, invitation to the Lord, heart as home, Guru's instruction.
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The speaker exonerates the Divine Husband, who bestows all peace, and instead blames her own bad deeds for the separation. She acknowledges that the Lord is flawless and that the distance between them is self-inflicted through negative actions. This is a confession of personal responsibility and a recognition that human error, not divine withholding, causes spiritual estrangement.

Themes: divine perfection, self-blame, bad karma, separation, spiritual estrangement, personal responsibility, peace-giver, husband-lord metaphor
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
The speaker urgently invites the Divine Teacher to enter the heart and dwell there, so that through the physical ears the listener may hear the Creator’s praise and glory. This is a plea for internal presence enabling external listening, a request for the Guru to inhabit the mind so that the ears become instruments for hearing the Lord’s virtues. It seeks the union of the guest within to facilitate the hearing of divine qualities without.

Themes: invitation to the Guru, divine indwelling, hearing the Lord's praise, internal sanctuary, spiritual listening, union of heart and sound, glorification of the Creator
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
The speaker urgently invites the Beloved Lord to enter and dwell within the heart, moving beyond a general request for presence to a specific plea for internal habitation. This intimate call expresses deep spiritual longing and the desire for the Divine to reside permanently within the mind, transforming the inner self into a home for the Beloved. It is an act of loving surrender and a request for the Lord to take possession of the devotee's being.

Themes: divine union, internalizing the divine, intimate prayer, longing for god, heart as sanctuary, beloved lord, spiritual habitation, surrender
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
The soul, personified as a forsaken wife, pleads with the Divine Husband to show mercy and take up residence within the heart. This is a desperate petition for grace, asking the Beloved to return to the home of the self and end the separation. It frames spiritual union as the Lord’s compassionate dwelling inside the devotee, emphasizing that the seeker’s only hope is the Master’s loving initiative and presence.

Themes: divine marriage metaphor, soul as bride, mercy, heart as sanctuary, longing for union, petition, grace, divine presence within.
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
The speaker pleads with the Fascinating Lord to enter and dwell within the home of the heart, transforming the physical body into a spiritual residence. This intimate invitation seeks the Divine presence inside the self, asking the Beloved to take up permanent residence within the inner being. The request is for an internal habitation of the Lord, turning the heart into a house where the Divine lives.

Themes: divine indwelling, heart as sanctuary, invitation to the Beloved, internal worship, longing for union, spiritual habitation, personal relationship with God, surrender of the self.
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The Divine Lord and Friend has manifested within the home of the heart, signifying an intimate inner union where the Beloved is no longer distant but present within the self. This declaration celebrates the arrival of the Divine Guest in the inner sanctuary, transforming the heart into a dwelling place for the Master and affirming that the true companion resides internally through spiritual realization.

Themes: divine immanence, inner union, heart as sanctuary, manifestation of the Lord, spiritual intimacy, presence of the beloved, internalization of the divine, arrival of the master.
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
Devotional worship performed during the first watch of the night is like a beautiful flower, but the true fruit only comes from the service done during the ambrosial hour before dawn. Early spiritual practice is attractive and preliminary, yet the substantial reward of amrit (immortal nectar) is reserved for the final, most sacred time of morning meditation. This metaphor distinguishes between the initial charm of discipline and its ultimate, ripening result.

Themes: ambrosial hour, amrit, early morning worship, spiritual ripening, stages of devotion, preliminary practice, ultimate reward, timing of prayer
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Kabeer is admonished for wasting human life in the deep slumber of maya (worldly attachment) instead of waking to perform simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine. The metaphor of sleep represents spiritual ignorance and intoxication with illusion, while rising signifies awakening to consciousness and the urgent need to remember the Lord before life passes. This rebuke demands immediate action to abandon the drowsiness of material delusion and engage in meditation on the Supreme Being.

Themes: spiritual awakening, maya as sleep, simran, urgency of human life, admonition of the self, divine remembrance, rejecting illusion, Murari as Lord.
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
Rise during the amrit vela, the ambrosial pre-dawn hours, to practice simran, the loving remembrance of the Divine Name. Fix the mind on the Guru’s feet, symbolizing total surrender and the internalization of the Guru’s wisdom. This instruction prioritizes early morning devotion, linking the chanting of God’s identity with deep humility and reverence for the enlightener who connects the seeker to that Divine reality.

Themes: amrit vela, simran, divine Name, Guru’s feet, surrender, early morning discipline, humility, internalization of wisdom.
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
Rise during the amrit vela, the pre-dawn ambrosial hour, to engage in jap, the repetition of the divine Name. This instruction commands the seeker to worship and adore the Lord continuously, extending the morning practice into constant remembrance day and night. The text establishes a discipline of unceasing devotion, urging the mind to remember the Creator at all times and transform fleeting ritual into perpetual loving awareness.

Themes: amrit vela, early rising, jap, naam, continuous remembrance, day and night worship, loving adoration, perpetual discipline.
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The rainbird calls out during the ambrosial hours before dawn, and this specific timing ensures its plea is accepted in the Divine Court. The image of the bird crying out represents the soul’s intense longing for union, while the early morning hour symbolizes the most auspicious time for spiritual practice. The text asserts that sincere prayer offered at this sacred time reaches the Lord directly, establishing a connection between disciplined devotion and divine acceptance.

Themes: rainbird, papiha, ambrosial hour, amrit vela, dawn, divine court, accepted prayer, spiritual longing, divine acceptance, timing of devotion
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing the virtues of the Lord of the Universe cools the scorching heart and brings peace to the mind. The act of chanting divine praise acts as a soothing balm that extinguishes inner burning and anxiety. Devotional singing creates a state of tranquility where the mind finds true happiness and relief from suffering through the cooling power of remembering the Divine.

Themes: cooling of the heart, inner peace, chanting divine virtues, relief from suffering, tranquility, emotional soothing, praise of the Lord, spiritual comfort
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing the praises of the Divine unites the consciousness with the Eternal, producing the state of yoga (spiritual union). This devotional singing grants the ascetic’s spiritual discipline and the householder’s worldly peace simultaneously. The act of vocalizing divine attributes becomes the method of absorption, merging the soul with the Beloved and granting all forms of contentment through the practice of kirtan (musical praise).

Themes: yoga, spiritual union, kirtan, singing praises, divine attributes, absorption, worldly peace, ascetic discipline
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
The speaker declares continuous engagement with the Divine through naam (the divine Name), performing kirtan (musical praise) without interruption from night to day. This practice signifies a state of perpetual remembrance and devotion, where the mind remains absorbed in singing the virtues of the Creator. The statement affirms an unbroken rhythm of worship, describing a life entirely dedicated to the constant repetition and glorification of God’s qualities.

Themes: continuous worship, kirtan, naam, divine praise, perpetual remembrance, unbroken devotion, absorption in God, glorification of the Lord
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Rise daily to join the sangat (company of the devout) and sing the sweet, melodious praises of the Divine. This practice involves vocalizing the anhad shabad (unstruck celestial sound) through the Guru’s words, transforming individual effort into a shared, rhythmic celebration of the Creator. The instruction emphasizes early rising and communal worship as the means to attune the mind to the eternal, internal music of naam (the divine Name) through devotional song.
Themes: early rising, sangat, anhad shabad, kirtan, communal worship, divine praise, simran, celestial sound
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
O holy saints, perpetually sing the glorious virtues of the Lord of the Universe. This direct command exhorts the devout to engage in the continuous vocalization of divine qualities, transforming praise into a constant state of being. The instruction emphasizes that spiritual life consists of unceasing adoration and the active remembrance of the Creator through the recitation of His attributes.

Themes: divine praise, continuous remembrance, glorification of the Lord, spiritual instruction, saintly conduct, vocal worship, Gobind, eternal adoration
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Sing the Creator's praises while free of desire, performing kirtan (devotional song) in the state of nirvaana (liberation from attachment). Remembering the Divine even for a single moment liberates the human being from all vices and inner corruptions. This instruction links inner purification with the act of singing, asserting that momentary remembrance of naam (the divine Name) secures total salvation and freedom from the cycle of birth and death.

Themes: nirvaana, liberation from vices, kirtan, momentary remembrance, naam, freedom from desire, salvation, singing praises
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The mind finds total satisfaction in every action of the Divine, accepting all outcomes as pleasing and benevolent. This stance of unwavering acceptance rejects any claim of personal ego or superiority, acknowledging that all praise belongs solely to the Creator. By surrendering the need to boast or elevate oneself, the devotee rests in the sweetness of divine will, finding even difficult circumstances agreeable because they originate from the beloved Lord.

Themes: radical acceptance, divine will, ego surrender, sweetness of hukam, inner satisfaction, rejection of pride, contentment in all circumstances
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
The Beloved Lord’s deeds appear as pure comfort and joy to the devotee, transforming all circumstances into sources of spiritual ease. This perspective reframes the Divine Friend’s actions as inherently benevolent, affirming that whatever the Creator does is pleasing and good. The speaker finds satisfaction in the Lord's working, accepting divine will as a state of grace rather than hardship.

Themes: divine will, acceptance, spiritual comfort, benevolence of the Lord, reframing hardship, inner satisfaction, surrender to the Friend
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Accepting the Divine Will as sweet brings total peace, joy, and auspiciousness. Surrendering to the Lord of the Universe results in every pleasure and happiness arriving. By internalizing God's will as agreeable, one attains a state of complete bliss and all positive circumstances manifest. This declaration affirms that aligning with the Creator's command is the source of all well-being and spiritual delight.

Themes: Divine Will, surrender, acceptance, inner peace, bliss, auspiciousness, alignment with God, spiritual joy
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The Divine instantly creates and destroys, exercising absolute power over existence and non-existence. This declaration emphasizes total sovereignty, asserting that the Creator alone decides the fate of all beings. Every decision rests within the Creator’s grip, signifying that no external force can alter the divine will. The imagery of hands holding all matters conveys complete control and the ultimate authority to establish or dismantle the universe at a mere whim.

Themes: divine sovereignty, creation and destruction, absolute control, divine will, transient existence, omnipotence, divine authority
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Meditating on naam (the divine Name) ensures that all worldly affairs are successfully resolved. The instruction emphasizes that constant remembrance of the Divine within the mind causes every task to reach its proper conclusion. By focusing loving remembrance on the Lord, one secures practical success and completion of all duties. This practice transforms spiritual devotion into tangible results, ensuring that no human effort remains unfulfilled when anchored in divine awareness.

Themes: naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), divine assistance, completion of tasks, practical success, mental focus, spiritual efficacy, worldly affairs
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
Continually singing the Glorious Praises of the Lord, Har, Har, Har, ensures that all personal affairs are perfectly resolved and brought to fruition. The speaker instructs their own mind to maintain this constant devotional singing as the practical means to secure successful outcomes, framing spiritual praise as the direct cause of worldly completion and the fulfillment of all necessary tasks.

Themes: divine praise, fulfillment of affairs, instruction to the mind, causal relationship between devotion and success, glorification of the Lord, completion of tasks, spiritual remedy for worldly needs.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Nanak declares that the primary human task is the worship of naam, the divine Name, asserting that through this loving remembrance, all worldly affairs and the ultimate purpose of life are successfully accomplished. This instruction establishes spiritual practice as the practical solution to every problem, ensuring that all business and duties find their resolution and fulfillment through the grace of simran.

Themes: naam, divine Name, simran, loving remembrance, resolution of affairs, life purpose, spiritual practice, grace, fulfillment of duties.
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
When the Divine is pleased, all worldly affairs are automatically resolved and arranged correctly. This line attributes the success of every task solely to divine will (raza), implying that human effort is futile without spiritual approval. It declares that external harmony is the direct result of internal acceptance by the Creator, meaning that when the Lord is benevolent, life’s complexities become simple and all obstacles vanish.

Themes: divine will, raza, surrender, grace, resolution of worldly affairs, divine pleasure, dependence on the Creator, automatic success
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
The speaker declares that every hope and desire is now completely fulfilled, resulting in a permanent state where sorrow can never arise again. This confident assertion describes the ultimate fruit of spiritual realization, where all needs are met by the Divine and the soul is liberated from pain. It affirms that complete inner satisfaction removes the very possibility of future suffering, establishing an unshakable condition of peace and fulfillment.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, cessation of sorrow, spiritual completion, liberation from pain, divine satisfaction, permanent bliss, inner contentment, realization of the Divine.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The beautiful lotus feet of the Divine serve as the sole foundation and refuge for the devotees, offering complete support and shelter. This image of surrender declares that spiritual life rests entirely upon the divine presence, which functions as the essential anchor and protection for the humble. The divine feet are both a concrete symbol of beauty and the ultimate source of stability for those seeking sanctuary.

Themes: divine refuge, surrender, spiritual support, lotus feet, sanctuary, foundation, divine protection, humility.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
The speaker resolves to fix the mind on the beautiful lotus feet of the Divine within the heart while relying entirely on the support of the Perfect Guru. This internal service of remembrance is sustained by the external anchor of the true guide, merging deep meditation with surrender to the teacher's refuge. The devotee rests their consciousness on the Lord's presence and depends on the Guru's strength to maintain that connection.

Themes: lotus feet, divine remembrance, heart sanctuary, perfect guru, refuge and support, internal meditation, reliance on the teacher, spiritual anchoring.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
Loving attachment to the Divine’s lotus feet constitutes the essential custom and established discipline that naturally fills the minds of the devout. This verse declares that cherishing the Lord’s presence is not a casual act but the defining way of life for the sangat, a spiritual practice that settles permanently within the consciousness of the holy. The imagery of lotus feet signifies both the beauty of the Divine and the state of total surrender and refuge.

Themes: divine love, spiritual discipline, sangat, lotus feet, surrender, refuge, internalization of faith, divine beauty
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
The mind is commanded to board the vessel of the Divine lotus feet to traverse the ocean of worldly existence. This metaphor treats the sanctuary of the Lord as a ship capable of ferrying the soul across the perilous sea of maya, offering the only means of safe passage to the far shore. Surrendering to the Guru’s refuge transforms the impossible crossing into a completed journey, liberating the devotee from the cycle of birth and death.

Themes: Divine sanctuary, ocean of worldliness, vessel of surrender, crossing over, liberation from transmigration, refuge in the Guru, spiritual passage, safety in devotion.
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
The mind is pierced and transfixed by the beautiful, soft lotus feet of the Divine, an image of total surrender and absorption. Once consciousness is penetrated by the Lord’s presence, worldly pleasures lose all flavor. Nothing else tastes sweet; only the Lord King remains delightful. The soul finds satisfaction exclusively in the Divine, rejecting all other sources of happiness as utterly bland compared to the nectar of naam (the divine Name).

Themes: lotus feet, piercing of the mind, exclusive sweetness, rejection of worldly pleasures, divine absorption, satisfaction in the Lord, spiritual longing, transcendence of maya.
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) brings deep spiritual satisfaction and ends all inner hunger. The Guru grants immortality, liberating the devotee from the cycle of birth and death. This state transcends physical aging and suffering, ensuring the soul never experiences decay or pain again. The act of internalizing divine wisdom transforms a mortal existence into eternal freedom.

Themes: immortality, ambrosial nectar, spiritual satisfaction, liberation from death, eternal life, cessation of suffering, Guru's grace, transcendence of aging
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Drinking the essence of naam (the divine Name) intoxicates the soul with spiritual ecstasy, severing all attachments to maya (worldly illusion). Consuming this divine nectar liberates the being, causing the fetters of transmigration to snap and the nooses of material bondage to break completely. This absorption in the Name results in a state of divine intoxication where all chains of existence are destroyed.

Themes: naam, divine intoxication, liberation, cutting bonds, maya, spiritual ecstasy, breaking shackles, essence of the Name
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The speaker urges the mind to drink the life-giving water of the divine Name, which is the true amrit (immortalizing nectar) of the Lord. This act of internal consumption grants spiritual life and sustenance, transforming the seeker from within. It is a direct plea to experience the essence of the Divine through simran (loving remembrance), tasting that which nourishes the soul and awakens it to its eternal nature.

ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru administers the life-giving water of naam (the divine Name) into the mouth, reviving a soul previously dead in spiritual ignorance. This act of grace transforms inner death into true life, awakening the spirit through the Guru’s instruction. The recipient, once lifeless without divine connection, is restored to existence by this ambrosial nectar. ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The Divine Name is a permanent storehouse of immortalizing nectar, a spiritual wealth that does not diminish. This instruction urges the listener to actively consume this essence through collective participation, specifically within the sangat (company of the devout), rather than hoarding it. The act of drinking symbolizes internalizing the naam (divine Name) to satisfy the soul's thirst, transforming the gathering into a feast of immortality where the divine treasure is shared and experienced directly.

ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The Divine eliminates the terror of birth and death for the devotee, severing the cycle of reincarnation so that the soul does not return to another womb. This liberation from transmigration signifies the end of suffering and the cessation of wandering through countless life forms. By removing the dread of mortality, the Supreme Being grants release from the painful wheel of coming and going, ensuring freedom from the bondage of repeated existence.

ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Attaining intuitive poise or sahaj (a state of natural, effortless spiritual equilibrium) results in realizing the Divine, which simultaneously eliminates the terror of the Messenger of Death. The text asserts that inner stability and the cessation of mental wavering are the direct causes of union with God, leading to a condition where spiritual death or the fear of dying cannot approach the devotee. Finding the Supreme Lord through unwavering composure removes all dread of mortality.

Themes: sahaj, intuitive poise, fear of death, realization of God, inner stability, union with the Divine, cessation of mental wavering, spiritual immortality
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Chanting the hymns of praise within the sangat (company of the devout) severs the terror of the cycle of reincarnation. The practice of reciting the sabad (divine Word) cuts away the lifelong dread of transmigration and the endless suffering of birth and death. Immersion in the Guru’s instruction destroys the primal fear of mortality, liberating the servant from the anxiety of existence and the bondage of coming and going.

Themes: sabad (divine Word), sangat (company of the devout), simran (loving remembrance), cycle of birth and death, fear of mortality, liberation, reincarnation, praise, cutting fear, chanting hymns, existential dread, spiritual practice.
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Meditating on the Divine eradicates the terror of the endless cycle of birth, aging, and death. Through loving remembrance, the anxiety surrounding physical mortality and the suffering of old age are entirely removed. This practice grants liberation from the existential dread inherent in transmigration, ensuring that the pain of worldly existence no longer afflicts the devotee.

Themes: simran, liberation from transmigration, fear of death, overcoming mortality, eradication of anxiety, protection from suffering, divine remembrance, cessation of pain
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
The company of the devout severs the lifelong suffering inherent in the cycle of reincarnation, cutting away the agony of birth and death. By eliminating the terror of the Messenger of Death, this spiritual association removes the dread of divine judgment and liberates the soul from the fear of dying. True sangat destroys the anxiety surrounding mortality and ends the bondage to worldly pain.

Themes: sangat, liberation from reincarnation, fear of death, removal of suffering, divine judgment, spiritual company, cutting bonds, mortality
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
The speaker declares that the terror of the cycle of reincarnation, the endless wheel of birth and death, has been entirely removed. This is a proclamation of liberation from existential dread, achieved through spiritual realization. The fear of dying and being reborn again has vanished, signifying a state of ultimate freedom where the soul is no longer bound by the anxieties of transmigration or the suffering inherent in worldly existence.

Themes: liberation from reincarnation, removal of existential fear, transcendence of birth and death, spiritual freedom, cessation of transmigration, divine grace, release from worldly anxiety
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Relying on the sanctuary of sangat (the company of the devout) allows one to become deeply enamored with the Divine, absorbing the Creator's color. This protective fellowship fosters an intimate spiritual union and infuses the being with the Lord's love. By taking shelter in the holy congregation, the individual soul merges completely with God, becoming dyed in the hue of the Beloved.

Themes: sangat (holy company), divine love, spiritual refuge, absorption in God, intimate union, divine color, reliance on the devout, emotional devotion.
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Remaining in the sangat (company of the devout) allows one to traverse the terrifying world-ocean of existence and sever the noose of the Messenger of Death. This line asserts that spiritual companionship is the essential vessel for liberation, cutting the bonds of mortality and attachment that bind the soul. By associating with holy beings, the impossible crossing becomes possible and the fear of dying is destroyed.

Themes: sangat (spiritual company), liberation, crossing the world-ocean, cutting the noose of death, fear of dying, bonds of maya, salvation through companionship.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Entering the sangat (company of the devout) causes immediate union with the Divine, framing spiritual companionship as the direct catalyst for meeting the Beloved. This instruction asserts that finding the holy assembly is synonymous with finding God, dissolving the distance between the seeker and the Lord through communal refuge. The act of joining the faithful results in merging with the Creator, making the congregation itself the vessel for divine union.

Themes: sangat (company of the devout), divine union, spiritual companionship, meeting the Lord, communal refuge, finding God through association, merging with the Creator.
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
Those who are perpetually united with the true congregation, or sangat, become dyed in the beautiful color of divine love, immersing themselves completely in the Lord's praise. This continuous absorption in the holy company transforms their inner state, coloring them with celestial affection so that they naturally sing the virtues of the Divine. Remaining forever linked to the assembly of the devout, they are imbued with a deep spiritual hue and devotedly celebrate the Creator's glory.

Themes: sangat, divine love, absorption, singing praises, spiritual transformation, perpetual connection, celestial color, true congregation
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
The speaker pleads with the Divine to be physically extracted from other toxic affairs and vices, acknowledging that the Creator actively engages the mind within sangat (the company of the devout). This prayer recognizes that liberation from worldly entanglement requires divine initiative, while simultaneously requesting that the consciousness be fixed upon the holy congregation. It frames spiritual rescue as a transition from diverse corruptions to the singular focus of the sacred gathering.

Themes: divine rescue, sangat (holy company), detachment from vice, fixing the mind, prayer for liberation, transition from corruption to devotion, divine initiative.
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
Hear the immense glory and greatness of the Saadh Sangat, the holy congregation or sangat (company of the devout). This proclamation urges the listener to recognize the supreme value found in the gathering of true devotees, where the divine presence is realized. The speaker calls out to friends to understand that spiritual elevation and the praise of the Divine are achieved through this sacred fellowship and collective worship.

Themes: sangat, holy congregation, spiritual community, divine glory, fellowship, collective worship, spiritual elevation, hearing the truth
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
The speaker identifies the Guru as the Transcendent Lord and the source of all comfort, equating the human guide with the Divine. This declaration asserts that true peace comes only from this supreme being, who bestows every kind of happiness. By merging the teacher with the Creator, the text emphasizes that the ultimate origin of tranquility and the provider of all bliss is one and the same entity.

Themes: Guru as God, source of peace, bestower of happiness, Transcendent Lord, divine comfort, equating guide with Creator, origin of bliss.
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
The Divine is addressed directly as the sole source of all creation, the pervasive presence within every being, and the generous bestower of gifts. This declaration identifies the Creator as the Architect of Destiny who writes the script of every life, emphasizing that all sustenance and existence flow exclusively from this one primal being. It affirms total dependence on the Creator who simultaneously gives, creates, and sustains all existence.

Themes: Creator as giver, architect of destiny, divine omnipresence, sole sustainer, dependence on the Divine, creation and providence, primal being, universal generosity.
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
The speaker addresses the Divine as the very form of mercy and the inexhaustible storehouse of grace, imploring this benevolent Lord to grant the sight of His presence. This vision of the Divine is not merely seeing but the bestowal of a redeemed, elevated spiritual existence. The act of beholding the Lord itself constitutes liberation and the ultimate status of life, transforming the seeker through the direct experience of divine compassion.

Themes: divine mercy, darshan (sight of the Divine), spiritual redemption, grace as treasure, elevated existence, compassionate Lord, liberation through sight.
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
The Divine is addressed as the sovereign master who is completely filled with all virtues and qualities, possessing a profound and unfathomable depth of heart or being. This declaration praises the Lord as the ultimate treasure of excellence, acknowledging that the Creator is the source of all goodness and possesses immense, deep spiritual capacity. The speaker affirms the Lord’s greatness and the vastness of divine character.

Themes: divine virtues, unfathomable depth, lordship, spiritual treasure, praise, divine excellence, greatness, completeness
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The Lord who gives sustenance to all living beings is the true Benefactor, yet no human mouth possesses the capacity to offer adequate praise or fully describe His virtues. This expression of humility acknowledges the infinite nature of divine generosity compared to the finite limits of language and speech. The speaker admits the impossibility of completing the Lord's simran (loving remembrance) or articulating His boundless qualities through any physical organ of speech.

Themes: divine generosity, inadequacy of human speech, infinite versus finite, humility before the Creator, impossibility of full praise, sustenance for all life, limits of language, simran
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The speaker expresses overwhelming inadequacy while attempting to praise the Divine, asking which specific virtues to sing because the Master is the limitless storehouse of all excellence. This rhetorical question highlights the infinite nature of divine qualities compared to finite human capacity, acknowledging the Lord as the owner and sustainer of all who embodies every possible perfection. The act of singing becomes impossible due to the sheer volume of glorious attributes.

Themes: divine virtues, infinite praise, rhetorical inadequacy, treasure of excellence, Lord and Master, sustainer, owner of all, glorification
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
This address rebukes the deluded self as a madman, declaring that no one will offer shelter or hospitality for even a single moment. The speaker warns that worldly attachments and relations provide no lasting refuge, emphasizing the absolute transience of human support. It exposes the futility of relying on others when death approaches, urging the mind to recognize its isolation and the fleeting nature of all external protection.

Themes: delusion, transience, lack of refuge, isolation, mortality, futility of worldly support, admonishment of the mind.
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
The speaker admonishes their own mind for wavering in doubt or instability, asserting that the Divine fulfills all hopes and desires. This rebuke commands the mind to cease its oscillation and trust that the Supreme Being satisfies every longing. It reframes the Lord as the complete fulfiller of wishes, urging the mind to abandon its restless vacillation and rely on the One who grants all boons and meets every need.

Themes: admonishing the mind, wavering doubt, fulfillment of desires, divine benevolence, trusting the Lord, inner instability, granting wishes, spiritual reassurance
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
O mind, you also must engage in bhajan (devotional worship) of the Supreme Being. This imperative command addresses the self directly, urging the internal faculties to cease wandering and instead focus entirely on the Lord of the Universe. It is an urgent call to shift from distraction to continuous remembrance, emphasizing that the mind itself must actively participate in loving devotion and meditation on the Divine.

Themes: internal command, bhajan, meditation, Lord of the Universe, addressing the mind, shifting focus, divine remembrance, urgent instruction
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
The speaker addresses their own mind, commanding it to stop seeking material objects or spiritual fulfillment in the external world because the true treasure, the Divine source of all happiness, already dwells within. This instruction redirects the search from outward rituals or possessions to the inner self, asserting that the ultimate wealth is internal residence rather than external acquisition. It admonishes the wandering mind for looking outside when the complete source of peace is already enshrined inside.

Themes: internal treasure, divine indwelling, cessation of external seeking, inner self, admonishing the mind, spiritual wealth within, redirecting focus inward, divine presence inside
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
Listen, you madman lost in the delusion of maya (worldly attachment). Why do you look upon this visible world and forget your true path, wandering astray from the purpose of human life? The speaker admonishes the self for becoming distracted by temporary sights, losing the way while staring at the illusion. It questions the foolishness of valuing fleeting appearances over spiritual reality, urging the mind to wake up from this intoxication of error.

Themes: maya, delusion, spiritual blindness, admonition of the mind, worldly distraction, forgetting the divine, human error, illusion versus reality
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
The speaker addresses the wandering mind as a madman, commanding it to become the dust under the feet of those who practice simran, the loving remembrance of the Divine. This metaphor of dust signifies total humility and the erasure of ego, urging the listener to seek the sangat, the company of the devout, and surrender completely to their spiritual superiority to attain union with the Lord.

Themes: humility, dust of the feet, sangat, simran, ego eradication, surrender, spiritual company, divine union
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
Receiving a single look of compassionate grace from the Satguru (True Guru) bestows spiritual wealth and joy surpassing the combined happiness of hundreds of thousands of earthly kings. The divine glance of nadar (grace) instantly elevates the devotee beyond all worldly sovereignty and princely comforts, transforming inner state through the Guru’s merciful attention. This unconditional favor grants supreme bliss that eclipses all material power and royal pleasures.
Themes: nadar (divine glance), grace of the guru, spiritual wealth, royal metaphor, supreme bliss, divine mercy, inner transformation, surpassing worldly power
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
Only when the Satguru (True Guru) bestows grace does suffering cease, not because hardship vanishes, but because the devotee no longer perceives it as pain. The merciful teacher transforms the inner experience of adversity, turning anguish into acceptance through spiritual vision. Divine compassion alters perception so that even worldly trouble feels harmless to the surrendered mind.

Themes: Satguru's mercy, cessation of suffering, transformation of perception, acceptance of divine will, spiritual vision, grace versus pain, inner detachment from hardship.
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The soul enters the fourth and final stage of spiritual union with the Divine, achieving a state of perfect stability and inner peace. This metaphor of marriage signifies total surrender and the consummation of love, where the individual self merges with the Beloved Lord. The mind, previously restless, becomes still and equipoised through divine grace, resulting in the ultimate realization of God and the cessation of all separation.

Themes: spiritual union, marriage ceremony metaphor, inner peace, sahaj (natural equipoise), divine grace, realization of God, stillness of mind, consummation of love
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Pleasing the True Guru brings deep peace and contentment, signifying that internalizing the Teacher within the heart yields all desired fruits. This statement links the act of gratifying the guide with the attainment of spiritual tranquility and complete fulfillment. By establishing the divine presence in the mind, one secures every desired result and finds lasting repose.

Themes: pleasing the True Guru, finding peace, internalizing the Teacher, attainment of desires, spiritual tranquility, contentment, divine presence in the heart, fulfillment
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The speaker declares the True Guru to be a perpetual helper who has severed the root of suffering, not merely its symptoms. This act of cutting the foundational stalk of pain signifies a permanent spiritual rescue rather than temporary relief. The text affirms that the Guru functions as an eternal support system, actively destroying the very source of anguish for those who seek sanctuary.

Themes: eternal support, severing the root of suffering, spiritual rescue, cutting the stalk of pain, True Guru as helper, sanctuary, destruction of anguish, permanent relief.
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
This statement presents human birth as a singular, fleeting opportunity to unite with the Divine Master, urging immediate action before the chance is lost. It frames the current moment as the decisive window for spiritual fulfillment, emphasizing that meeting the Lord of the Universe is the specific purpose of this life. The text warns against wasting this rare occasion, asserting that union with the Supreme Soul is the ultimate goal and that this specific existence provides the only means to achieve it.

Themes: human birth as opportunity, union with the Divine, urgency of spiritual practice, purpose of life, fleeting nature of time, meeting the Lord of the Universe, rare chance for salvation.
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
The speaker addresses the mortal being, declaring that human birth is not an accident but a commercial opportunity intended solely for spiritual gain. This incarnation is a specific transaction where one must earn the profit of naam (the divine Name), turning worldly existence into a venture for accumulating true wealth rather than material loss. The text frames life as a purposeful arrival to harvest divine blessings, urging the listener to recognize this rare chance for spiritual commerce and secure eternal value through devotion.

Themes: human purpose, spiritual profit, naam (the divine Name), life as transaction, earning divine wealth, rare opportunity, commercial metaphor, spiritual gain
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Meeting the true Guru implants firm devotion to the Divine within the heart, establishing an unshakable spiritual foundation. This internalized worship is the only endeavor that will ultimately succeed or bear fruit, rendering all other worldly pursuits useless. The instruction emphasizes that encountering the holy sangat and solidifying loving remembrance inside oneself constitutes the sole effective action for human life.

Themes: meeting the Guru, implanted devotion, firm bhagti, internal worship, spiritual foundation, sole effective action, futility of worldly pursuits, divine realization.
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
True success in human existence belongs to those who listen to the divine Name and then live by constantly chanting it in loving remembrance. This practice of hearing and repeating the Lord’s Name transforms ordinary living into spiritual fulfillment, granting eternal life. The repetition of jap (meditative recitation) emphasizes that continuous engagement with the divine is the only way to make life fruitful and permanent.
Themes: successful life, hearing the divine Name, jap (meditative recitation), simran (loving remembrance), eternal life, chanting, spiritual fulfillment, constant remembrance.
